186.question: For 𝑋1, … , 𝑋𝑛∼Pareto(𝜃), 𝑓(𝑥; 𝜃) = 𝜃/𝑥𝜃+1, 𝑥> 1, UMVUE of 𝜃is:

191.title: Rao Blackwell Normal
191.question: For 𝑋1, … , 𝑋𝑛∼𝑁(𝜇, 𝜎2) with 𝜎2 known, improve 𝑇0 = 𝑋²_1 −𝜎2 (unbiased for 𝜇2) using 𝑆=̄ 𝑋:

Exist only for 𝜉< 1/3 (finite third moment required)
Are always less efficient than MLE

207.question: For 𝑋1, … , 𝑋𝑛∼𝑈(0, 𝜃), exact one-sided CI for 𝜃based on 𝑋(𝑛) is:

250.explanation: Single bootstrap CI: coverage error 𝑂(𝑛−1/2); double bootstrap: 𝑂(𝑛−1); studentized bootstrap also achieves 𝑂(𝑛−1); computationally expensive

251.title: NP Lemma Statement

251.question: Neyman-Pearson lemma: Most powerful test of size 𝛼for 𝐻0 ∶𝜃= 𝜃0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜃= 𝜃1 rejects when:
options: Λ = 𝑓(𝑥; 𝜃1)/𝑓(𝑥; 𝜃0) > 𝑘where 𝑘chosen so 𝑃𝐻0(Λ > 𝑘) = 𝛼
251.explanation: Ratio is 𝑓1/𝑓0 (alternative over null); reject for LARGE ratio; B has ratio inverted; k determined by size constraint

252.title: UMP Exponential Family
252.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
252.question: For one-parameter exponential family with monotone likelihood ratio in 𝑇(𝑥), UMP test of 𝐻0 ∶𝜃≤𝜃0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜃> 𝜃0:
252.explanation: If LR is increasing in 𝑇: reject for large 𝑇; if decreasing: reject for small 𝑇; must check direction

253.title: UMP Existence Two Sided

253.question: UMP test for two-sided 𝐻1 ∶𝜃≠𝜃0 against one-sided 𝐻0 ∶𝜃= 𝜃0:
253.explanation: UMP for two-sided alternatives generally fails; the test that is MP against 𝜃1 > 𝜃0 differs from MP against 𝜃1 < 𝜃0; UMPU tests exist instead

254.title: NP Lemma Normal Mean
254.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
254.question: For 𝑋1, … , 𝑋𝑛∼𝑁(𝜇, 𝜎2) with 𝜎2 known, MP test of 𝐻0 ∶𝜇= 𝜇0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜇= 𝜇1 > 𝜇0:
options: Reject if̄ 𝑋> 𝑐where 𝑐= 𝜇0 + 𝑧𝛼𝜎/√𝑛
254.explanation: LR= exp[𝑛(𝜇1 −𝜇0)̄𝑋/𝜎2 −const]; increasing in̄ 𝑋(since 𝜇1 > 𝜇0); reject for large 𝑋; 𝑐from size constraint

255.title: Power Function Definition

255.question: Power function 𝛽(𝜃) of a test is:
255.explanation: Power function defined for ALL 𝜃; under 𝐻0: 𝛽(𝜃) = 𝛼(size); under 𝐻1: 𝛽(𝜃) = power; C is incomplete

256.title: Critical Region Types
256.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
256.question: For testing 𝐻0 ∶𝜇= 𝜇0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜇≠𝜇0 (normal, 𝜎known), critical region is:
256.explanation: Two-sided test: A and D are equivalent; B is one-sided right; C is one-sided left; for two-sided, use 𝑧𝛼/2 not 𝑧𝛼

257.title: Similar Region
257.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
257.question: A critical region 𝐶is similar of size 𝛼if:
257.explanation: Similar region: EXACTLY 𝛼for all 𝜃∈𝐻0 (not just ≤𝛼); level 𝛼test has ≤𝛼; similar tests are useful for composite 𝐻0

258.title: Unbiased Test
258.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
258.question: A test is unbiased if:
options: 𝛽(𝜃) ≥𝛼for all 𝜃∈𝐻1 and 𝛽(𝜃) ≤𝛼for all 𝜃∈𝐻0
Type I error equals Type II error
258.explanation: Unbiased: power under 𝐻1 is at least as large as size; ensures test is not “worse than random”; B is similar test; D is unrelated

259.title: Randomized Test
259.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
259.question: A randomized test with critical function 𝜙(𝑥) means:
259.explanation: Randomized test: 𝜙(𝑥) = 𝑃(reject|𝑋= 𝑥); needed to achieve exact size 𝛼for discrete distributions; 𝜙(𝑥) ∈{0, 1} for non-randomized

260.title: NP Lemma Poisson
260.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
260.question: For 𝑋∼Poisson(𝜆), MP test of 𝐻0 ∶𝜆= 𝜆0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜆= 𝜆1 > 𝜆0:
260.explanation: LR= (𝜆1/𝜆0)𝑥𝑒−(𝜆1−𝜆0); increasing in 𝑥(since 𝜆1 > 𝜆0); reject for large 𝑋; randomization at boundary for exact size

261.title: UMP Normal Variance
261.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
261.question: For 𝑋1, … , 𝑋𝑛∼𝑁(𝜇, 𝜎2) with 𝜇known, UMP test of 𝐻0 ∶𝜎2 ≤𝜎²_0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜎2 > 𝜎²_0:
261.explanation: ∑(𝑋𝑖−𝜇)2/𝜎2 ∼𝜒²_𝑛; MLR in ∑(𝑋𝑖−𝜇)2; reject for large values; 𝜇known is crucial

262.title: Power Calculation Normal
262.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
262.question: For 𝐻0 ∶𝜇= 0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜇= 𝛿> 0 with 𝜎known, power of 𝑧-test at level 𝛼is:
262.explanation: Power= 𝑃(̄𝑋> 𝑧𝛼𝜎/√𝑛|𝜇= 𝛿) = 𝑃(𝑍> 𝑧𝛼−𝛿√𝑛/𝜎) = 1 −Φ(𝑧𝛼−𝛿√𝑛/𝜎) = Φ(𝛿√𝑛/𝜎−𝑧𝛼); A and C equivalent

263.title: NP Lemma Exponential
263.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
263.question: For 𝑋1, … , 𝑋𝑛∼Exp(𝜃), MP test of 𝐻0 ∶𝜃= 𝜃0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜃= 𝜃1 < 𝜃0 (smaller rate = larger mean):
263.explanation: LR= (𝜃1/𝜃0)𝑛exp[−(𝜃1 −𝜃0) ∑𝑥𝑖]; since 𝜃1 < 𝜃0: −(𝜃1 −𝜃0) > 0; LR increasing in ∑𝑥𝑖; reject for large ∑𝑋𝑖

264.title: UMP One Sided Composite
264.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
264.question: For 𝐻0 ∶𝜃≤𝜃0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜃> 𝜃0 in exponential family with MLR in 𝑇(𝑥):
options: UMP test rejects for 𝑇(𝑥) > 𝑐where 𝑐satisfies sup𝜃≤𝜃0 𝑃𝜃(𝑇> 𝑐) = 𝛼
UMP test rejects for 𝑇(𝑥) < 𝑐
UMP does not exist for composite 𝐻0
264.explanation: MLR property: test that is MP for each simple 𝜃1 > 𝜃0 is the same test; this common test is UMP; size achieved at 𝜃= 𝜃0 (boundary)

265.title: Neyman Pearson Randomized
265.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
265.question: When 𝑃𝐻0(Λ > 𝑘) = 𝛼1 < 𝛼< 𝛼2 = 𝑃𝐻0(Λ ≥𝑘), the NP test randomizes at Λ = 𝑘with probability:
265.explanation: Randomization probability 𝛾chosen so total size= 𝛼1 + 𝛾(𝛼2 −𝛼1) = 𝛼; solving gives A; needed for discrete distributions

266.title: Power Function Monotone
266.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
266.question: For UMP test in exponential family with MLR, power function 𝛽(𝜃) is:
options: Monotone increasing in 𝜃(for one-sided 𝐻1 ∶𝜃> 𝜃0)
266.explanation: MLR implies monotone power function; this is the key property that makes the test UMP; power increases as 𝜃moves further into 𝐻1

267.title: Most Powerful Level
267.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
267.question: A test is most powerful of level 𝛼(not size 𝛼) if:
267.explanation: Level 𝛼: size ≤𝛼(inequality); size 𝛼: size = 𝛼(equality); MP of level 𝛼may have size < 𝛼(conservative)

268.title: NP Lemma Uniform
268.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
268.question: For 𝑋∼𝑈(0, 𝜃), testing 𝐻0 ∶𝜃= 1 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜃= 2, MP test:
options: Rejects if 𝑋> 𝑐for some 𝑐∈(0, 1)
Always rejects (since 𝐻1 support contains 𝐻0 support)
268.explanation: 𝑓(𝑥; 2)/𝑓(𝑥; 1) = 1/2 for 𝑥∈(0, 1) and ∞for 𝑥∈(1, 2); always reject if 𝑋> 1; for 𝑋≤1, LR= 1/2 (constant); randomize to achieve exact size 𝛼

269.title: UMP Bernoulli
269.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
269.question: For 𝑋1, … , 𝑋𝑛∼Bernoulli(𝑝), UMP test of 𝐻0 ∶𝑝≤𝑝0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝑝> 𝑝0:
269.explanation: Bernoulli is exponential family with MLR in ∑𝑋𝑖; UMP rejects for large ∑𝑋𝑖; critical value from Bin(𝑛, 𝑝0) distribution

270.title: Power Envelope
270.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
270.question: The power envelope is:
options: Maximum achievable power at each 𝜃∈𝐻1 over all level-𝛼tests
Power of the likelihood ratio test
Both A and B when UMP exists
270.explanation: Power envelope = upper bound on power; when UMP exists, it achieves the envelope; when UMP doesn’t exist, no single test achieves the envelope everywhere

271.title: NP Lemma Composite H1
271.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
271.question: NP lemma directly applies to:
options: Simple 𝐻0 vs simple 𝐻1 only
271.explanation: NP lemma: both hypotheses must be simple (point hypotheses); extension to composite uses UMP theory (MLR, exponential family); LRT handles general composite

272.title: Similar Test Construction
272.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
272.question: For composite 𝐻0 ∶𝜃∈Θ0, similar tests of size 𝛼are constructed using:
options: Neyman structure: 𝐸𝜃[𝜙(𝑋)|𝑇(𝑋)] = 𝛼for sufficient statistic 𝑇under 𝐻0
272.explanation: Neyman structure: conditional on sufficient statistic for nuisance parameter, test has constant conditional size 𝛼; this gives similar tests

273.title: UMP Unbiased Two Sided
273.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
273.question: UMPU test for 𝐻0 ∶𝜃= 𝜃0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜃≠𝜃0 in exponential family:
options: Rejects for 𝑇< 𝑐1 or 𝑇> 𝑐2 with 𝑐1, 𝑐2 chosen for size and unbiasedness
Is the same as the two-sided 𝑧-test always
273.explanation: UMPU: two critical values 𝑐1 < 𝑐2; conditions: 𝐸𝜃0[𝜙] = 𝛼(size) and 𝐸𝜃0[𝑇𝜙] = 𝛼𝐸𝜃0[𝑇] (unbiasedness); for normal, reduces to equal-tails 𝑧-test

274.title: Power Sample Size
274.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
274.question: To achieve power 1 −𝛽at 𝜇= 𝜇1 for one-sided 𝑧-test at level 𝛼, required 𝑛is:
274.explanation: Power= Φ(𝛿√𝑛/𝜎−𝑧𝛼) = 1 −𝛽; so 𝛿√𝑛/𝜎= 𝑧𝛼+ 𝑧𝛽; squaring: A; D uses 𝑧𝛼/2 (two-sided)

275.title: NP Lemma Sufficient Stat
275.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
275.question: When sufficient statistic 𝑇exists, NP lemma critical region can be expressed in terms of 𝑇because:
options: Likelihood ratio is a function of 𝑇only
275.explanation: By factorization theorem, 𝑓(x; 𝜃) = 𝑔(𝑇; 𝜃)ℎ(x); LR= 𝑔(𝑇; 𝜃1)/𝑔(𝑇; 𝜃0); depends on x only through 𝑇

276.title: Power Function Beta Distribution
276.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
276.question: For 𝑋∼Beta(𝜃, 1), testing 𝐻0 ∶𝜃= 1 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜃= 2, power of MP test at level 𝛼:
276.explanation: 𝑓(𝑥; 𝜃) = 𝜃𝑥𝜃−1; LR= 2𝑥/1 = 2𝑥; reject for large 𝑥; 𝑃(𝑋> 𝑐|𝜃= 1) = 1 −𝑐= 𝛼; 𝑐= 1 −𝛼; power= 𝑃(𝑋> 1 −𝛼|𝜃= 2) = 1 −(1 −𝛼)2

277.title: UMP Scale Family
277.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
277.question: For scale family(1)/(𝜃𝑓)(𝑥/𝜃) with 𝑓log-concave, UMP test of 𝐻0 ∶𝜃≤𝜃0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜃> 𝜃0:
options: Rejects for large 𝑋(𝑛) (if 𝑓is uniform)
277.explanation: Sufficient statistic and rejection region depend on the specific scale family; exponential: ∑𝑋𝑖; uniform: 𝑋(𝑛); no universal answer

278.title: Critical Region Composite

278.question: For composite 𝐻0 ∶𝜇≥𝜇0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜇< 𝜇0 (normal, 𝜎known), level-𝛼test:
278.explanation: One-sided left test; size achieved at 𝜇= 𝜇0 (boundary of 𝐻0); use 𝑧𝛼not 𝑧𝛼/2; B is right-sided; C is two-sided

279.title: Power Function Continuity
279.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
279.question: Power function 𝛽(𝜃) of a test based on continuous data is:
options: May be discontinuous for discrete distributions
279.explanation: For continuous data, power function is continuous (and often differentiable) in 𝜃; for discrete data, power function may have jumps; A is correct for continuous case

280.title: NP Lemma Multiparameter
280.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
280.question: For multiparameter family, NP lemma:
options: Applies directly to simple vs simple hypotheses
280.explanation: NP lemma applies to any simple vs simple hypothesis regardless of dimension; the LR test is MP; extension to composite is harder in multiparameter case

281.title: UMP Exponential Rate
281.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
281.question: For 𝑋1, … , 𝑋𝑛∼Exp(𝜃) (rate), UMP test of 𝐻0 ∶𝜃= 𝜃0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜃> 𝜃0:
options: Reject for small ∑𝑋𝑖(large rate = small mean)
281.explanation: Large rate 𝜃means small mean 1/𝜃; LR increasing in −∑𝑋𝑖(or decreasing in ∑𝑋𝑖); reject for SMALL ∑𝑋𝑖; common sign error

282.title: Power Function Normal Two Sided
282.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
282.question: Power function of two-sided 𝑧-test for 𝐻0 ∶𝜇= 0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜇≠0:
282.explanation: Two-sided: power = P(reject left) + P(reject right); for 𝜇> 0: left tail negligible; A is exact; B and C are one-sided approximations

283.title: Similar Region Exponential Family
283.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
283.question: In exponential family 𝑓(𝑥; 𝜃, 𝜆) = ℎ(𝑥) exp[𝜂1(𝜃)𝑇1 + 𝜂2(𝜆)𝑇2 −𝐵], similar test for 𝐻0 ∶𝜃= 𝜃0 (nuisance 𝜆) conditions on:
283.explanation: Condition on sufficient statistic for nuisance parameter 𝜆; conditional distribution of 𝑇1|𝑇2 is free of 𝜆; gives similar test

284.title: UMP Double Exponential
284.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
284.question: For 𝑋1, … , 𝑋𝑛∼Laplace(𝜃, 1), UMP test of 𝐻0 ∶𝜃= 0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜃> 0:
284.explanation: Laplace is NOT exponential family (absolute value in exponent); no MLR in simple statistic; UMP does not exist; sign test or Wilcoxon are used

285.title: Power Function Beta Calculation
285.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
285.question: For 𝑋∼Bin(10, 𝑝), test 𝐻0 ∶𝑝= 0.5 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝑝> 0.5, reject if 𝑋≥8. Power at 𝑝= 0.7:
285.explanation: Power at 𝑝= 0.7: compute under 𝐻1; A and C are equivalent expressions; B is the size (under 𝐻0)

286.title: NP Lemma Gamma
286.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
286.question: For 𝑋1, … , 𝑋𝑛∼Γ(𝛼, 𝜃) with 𝛼known, MP test of 𝐻0 ∶𝜃= 𝜃0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜃= 𝜃1 < 𝜃0:
286.explanation: Γ(𝛼, 𝜃) with scale 𝜃: 𝑓∝𝜃−𝑛𝛼exp(−∑𝑥𝑖/𝜃); LR= (𝜃0/𝜃1)𝑛𝛼exp[−∑𝑥𝑖(1/𝜃1 − 1/𝜃0)]; since 𝜃1 < 𝜃0: 1/𝜃1 > 1/𝜃0; LR decreasing in ∑𝑥𝑖; reject for SMALL ∑𝑋𝑖

287.title: UMP Normal Mean Variance Unknown
287.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
287.question: For 𝑁(𝜇, 𝜎2) with 𝜎2 unknown, UMP test of 𝐻0 ∶𝜇≤𝜇0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜇> 𝜇0:
287.explanation: With nuisance 𝜎2, UMP doesn’t exist in general; BUT the 𝑡-test is UMPU (uniformly most powerful unbiased); A is UMPU, not UMP; C is technically correct for UMP

288.title: Power Function Increasing
288.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
288.question: For one-sided test in exponential family, power function is strictly increasing because:
options: MLR property implies power is monotone in 𝜃
288.explanation: MLR ⇒monotone power function; this is the fundamental connection between MLR and UMP tests; completeness is separate

289.title: NP Lemma Composite Reduction
289.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
289.question: For composite 𝐻1 ∶𝜃> 𝜃0 in exponential family, UMP test is found by:
options: Applying NP lemma to each simple 𝐻1 ∶𝜃= 𝜃1 and noting the MP test is the same for all 𝜃1 > 𝜃0
289.explanation: Key insight: MLR ensures the NP critical region (reject for large 𝑇) is the same for ALL 𝜃1 > 𝜃0; this common test is UMP

290.title: Critical Region Randomized Discrete
290.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
290.question: For 𝑋∼Bin(5, 𝑝), testing 𝐻0 ∶𝑝= 0.5 at level 𝛼= 0.05, exact size requires:
options: Randomization at boundary since 𝑃(𝑋≥5|𝑝= 0.5) = 1/32 < 0.05 < 𝑃(𝑋≥4|𝑝= 0.5) = 6/32
290.explanation: Exact size 0.05 requires randomization: reject if 𝑋= 5; reject with prob 𝛾if 𝑋= 4; 𝛾= (0.05 −1/32)/(6/32 −1/32) = (0.05 −0.03125)/0.15625

291.title: UMP Negative Binomial
291.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
291.question: For 𝑋1, … , 𝑋𝑛∼NegBin(𝑟, 𝑝) with 𝑟known, UMP test of 𝐻0 ∶𝑝≥𝑝0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝑝< 𝑝0:
291.explanation: NegBin: 𝐸[𝑋] = 𝑟(1−𝑝)/𝑝; smaller 𝑝means larger mean; LR in ∑𝑋𝑖; for 𝑝1 < 𝑝0: reject for large ∑𝑋𝑖; A and C equivalent

292.title: Power Function Envelope Calculation
292.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
292.question: Power envelope at 𝜃1 for testing 𝐻0 ∶𝜃= 𝜃0 at level 𝛼is:
options: Power of NP MP test at 𝜃1
1 −𝛽where 𝛽is Type II error of best test
292.explanation: All three definitions are equivalent; NP lemma gives the test achieving the envelope; power envelope is the theoretical maximum

293.title: Similar Region Normal
293.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
293.question: For 𝑁(𝜇, 𝜎2) with both unknown, similar test of 𝐻0 ∶𝜇= 𝜇0 conditions on:
293.explanation: Under 𝐻0 ∶𝜇= 𝜇0, 𝑆2 is sufficient for 𝜎2; conditioning on 𝑆2 gives 𝑡-statistic with 𝑡𝑛−1 distribution free of 𝜎2; this gives the 𝑡-test as UMPU

294.title: UMP Pareto
294.topic: Neyman–Pearson Lemma, UMP Tests & Power Functions
294.question: For 𝑋1, … , 𝑋𝑛∼Pareto(𝜃), 𝑓(𝑥; 𝜃) = 𝜃/𝑥𝜃+1, 𝑥> 1, UMP test of 𝐻0 ∶𝜃≤𝜃0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜃> 𝜃0:

299.title: NP Lemma Sufficient Reduction

The critical region cannot be simplified

311.question: Likelihood ratio test statistic Λ is:

312.question: Under 𝐻0 and regularity conditions, −2 log Λ 𝑑−→:

313.question: For 𝑁(𝜇, 𝜎2) with both unknown, LRT of 𝐻0 ∶𝜇= 𝜇0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜇≠𝜇0:

314.title: SPRT Definition

314.question: Wald’s SPRT continues sampling while:
options: 𝐵< Λ𝑚< 𝐴where Λ𝑚= ∏ 𝑚 𝑖=1 𝑓(𝑋𝑖; 𝜃1)/𝑓(𝑋𝑖; 𝜃0)
314.explanation: SPRT: continue if 𝐵< Λ𝑚< 𝐴; stop and reject 𝐻0 if Λ𝑚≥𝐴; stop and accept 𝐻0 if Λ𝑚≤𝐵

315.explanation: 𝐴= (1 −𝛽)/𝛼(upper boundary for rejecting 𝐻0); 𝐵= 𝛽/(1 −𝛼) (lower boundary for accepting 𝐻0); these are approximate (ignore overshoot)

316.title: SPRT Normal

316.question: For 𝑋𝑖∼𝑁(𝜃, 1), SPRT of 𝐻0 ∶𝜃= 0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜃= 𝛿, log-LR after 𝑚observations:
316.explanation: log Λ𝑚= ∑[log 𝑓(𝑋𝑖; 𝛿) −log 𝑓(𝑋𝑖; 0)] = 𝛿∑𝑋𝑖−𝑚𝛿2/2; linear in ∑𝑋𝑖; SPRT reduces to boundary on ∑𝑋𝑖

317.topic: Likelihood Ratio Tests, SPRT & Decision Theory
317.question: Operating Characteristic (OC) function 𝐿(𝜃) of SPRT is:
317.explanation: OC function = probability of accepting 𝐻0; 𝐿(𝜃0) = 1 −𝛼; 𝐿(𝜃1) = 𝛽; power function= 1 −𝐿(𝜃); C is ASN function

318.title: ASN Function

318.question: ASN (Average Sample Number) function 𝐸𝜃[𝑁] for SPRT satisfies Wald’s identity:

319.title: SPRT Optimality

319.question: Wald-Wolfowitz theorem states SPRT is optimal in that:

SPRT minimizes maximum expected sample size
SPRT is UMP among sequential tests

320.title: LRT Composite Both

options: Λ = supΘ0 𝐿/ supΘ 𝐿; reject for small Λ
Λ = supΘ1 𝐿/ supΘ0 𝐿; reject for large Λ
Λ = 𝐿(̂𝜃0)/𝐿(̂𝜃); reject for small Λ
320.explanation: A and C are equivalent; supΘ 𝐿= max(supΘ0 𝐿, supΘ1 𝐿); when̂ 𝜃∉Θ0, supΘ 𝐿= 𝐿(̂𝜃); reject for small Λ (large −2 log Λ)

321.title: Decision Theory Loss

321.question: In decision theory, risk function 𝑅(𝜃, 𝑑) is:

322.title: Decision Theory Admissibility

322.question: Estimator 𝑑1 dominates 𝑑2 if:
options: 𝑅(𝜃, 𝑑1) ≤𝑅(𝜃, 𝑑2) for all 𝜃with strict inequality for some 𝜃
𝑅(𝜃, 𝑑1) < 𝑅(𝜃, 𝑑2) for all 𝜃
𝑅(𝜃, 𝑑1) ≤𝑅(𝜃, 𝑑2) for all 𝜃
322.explanation: Dominance: ≤everywhere AND < somewhere; B is too strong (strict everywhere); C allows equality everywhere (no dominance); D is minimax comparison

323.title: Minimax Estimator

323.question: Minimax estimator minimizes:
options: 𝑅(𝜃0, 𝑑) at a specific 𝜃0

324.question: Bayes estimator under squared error loss is:

326.explanation: Saturated model: 𝑟𝑐−1 free parameters; independence model: (𝑟−1) + (𝑐−1) free parameters; difference= (𝑟−1)(𝑐−1); this is the df for 𝜒2

327.question: Bayes risk of estimator 𝑑w.r.t. prior 𝜋is:

𝑟(𝜋, 𝑑) = 𝐸[𝐿(𝜃, 𝑑(𝑋))] over joint distribution
327.explanation: A and D are equivalent (both are expectation of loss over joint distribution of (𝜃, 𝑋)); B is minimax risk; Bayes estimator minimizes A=D

328.title: SPRT Exponential

328.question: For 𝑋𝑖∼Exp(𝜃) (rate), SPRT of 𝐻0 ∶𝜃= 𝜃0 vs 𝐻1 ∶𝜃= 𝜃1 > 𝜃0, SPRT boundary on ∑𝑋𝑖:

351.question: Under 0-1 loss 𝐿(𝜃, 𝑑) = 𝐼(𝜃≠𝑑), Bayes estimator is:

352.title: LRT Multivariate Normal
